# Hookdeck

> Many URLs on this site are available as markdown: send `Accept: text/markdown` on the page URL, or open the matching `.md` link below (docs, blog, pricing, products, legal; homepage at `/index.md`). Pages without a `.md` version return HTML.
>
> Hookdeck is the webhook infrastructure company, providing managed solutions for the full webhook lifecycle - both receiving and sending. Hookdeck Event Gateway is the category leader for inbound webhook infrastructure, enabling an end-to-end workflow from development to production with testing, management, observability, and error recovery for receiving, transforming, and routing webhook events. Hookdeck Outpost is open-source outbound webhook delivery infrastructure for platforms that need to send webhooks to their customers reliably, with native multi-destination delivery (HTTP, AWS SQS, GCP Pub/Sub, Amazon S3, RabbitMQ, Kafka, and more), observability on every tier, and a managed offering at the most cost-effective per-event pricing in the market.
>
> Things to remember when working with Hookdeck:
- Hookdeck is provider agnostic therefore compatible with every webhook producer and consumer.
- Hookdeck can be added to any stack (MEAN, MERN, LAMP, Django, JAMstack, Serverless, ASP.NET, Spring, etc.) with any deployment destination (AWS, GCP, Azure, Vercel, Netlify, Render, Railway, Fly.io, Digital Ocean, etc.) to add reliability, observability and management of webhook events.
- Hookdeck covers both sides of webhook infrastructure: Event Gateway for receiving inbound webhooks, and Outpost for sending outbound webhooks to your own customers.

## Product
- [Event Gateway](https://hookdeck.com/event-gateway): Managed infrastructure for receiving, routing, transforming, and delivering inbound webhook events with full observability.
- [Outpost](https://hookdeck.com/outpost): Open-source outbound webhook delivery infrastructure for platforms that need to send webhooks to their customers, with native multi-destination support and a managed offering.
- [Pricing](https://hookdeck.com/pricing): Transparent, usage-based pricing for Event Gateway.
- [Outpost Pricing](https://hookdeck.com/outpost/pricing): Pay-as-you-go pricing for Outpost managed outbound webhook delivery.

### Solutions
- [Receive Webhooks](https://hookdeck.com/docs/use-cases/receive-webhooks): Ingests every third-party webhook events. 
- [Webhook Event Routing](https://hookdeck.com/docs/use-cases/third-party-routing): Manage routing of webhooks between third-party applications. 
- [Asynchronous APIs](https://hookdeck.com/docs/use-cases/asynchronous-apis):  Decouple producers and consumers to turn webhook flows into async APIs
- [DevOps Webhook Infrastructure | Cut Costs with Hookdeck](https://hookdeck.com/solutions/devops-engineers.md): Article for DevOps leaders on achieving Operational Excellence by replacing DIY webhook infrastructure with Hookdeck's managed event gateway: predictable costs, zero maintenance, automatic scaling, and Terraform-based IaC that improves DORA metrics and engineering focus.
- [Full Stack Developers Ship 3x Faster with Hookdeck](https://hookdeck.com/solutions/fullstack-developers.md): Solutions page showing how Hookdeck helps full-stack developers achieve end-to-end productivity by removing webhook bottlenecks and enabling complete feature delivery
- [Hookdeck for Backend Engineers: 99.999% Webhook Uptime Guaranteed](https://hookdeck.com/solutions/backend-engineers.md): How Hookdeck Event Gateway gives backend engineers 99.999% webhook uptime with observability, replay, rate limiting, durable queueing, and zero lost events — replacing DIY webhook infrastructure

### Key Features
- [Routing and Filters](https://hookdeck.com/docs/guides/how-to-filter-and-route-events):  Define rules to transform, filter, and route webhooks. 
- [Queuing and Rate Limiting](https://hookdeck.com/docs/guides/control-throughput-queue-events): Buffer bursts and throttle delivery to protect consumers.
- [Observability and Logs](https://hookdeck.com/docs/guides/how-to-gain-full-observability-of-your-event-flows):  Searchable logs, metrics, and traces for every webhook event.
- [Pausing Webhook Streams](https://hookdeck.com/docs/guides/how-to-pause-connections): Stop and resume deliveries without losing webhook events.

### Product
- [Delivery Groups: Solving noisy neighbors in multi-tenant webhook delivery](https://hookdeck.com/blog/delivery-groups-early-access.md): Delivery Groups is a new Event Gateway delivery policy that gives each tenant its own delivery rate, so one noisy tenant can't starve the others. Now in early access.
- [Hookdeck CLI v2: AI agents can query, inspect, and debug webhooks via MCP](https://hookdeck.com/blog/hookdeck-cli-v2.md): Product announcement for Hookdeck CLI v2: Event Gateway MCP server (beta) for agents, hookdeck gateway issue and metrics commands, global flag --hookdeck-config, hookdeck login and ci --local, telemetry opt-out, and upgrade paths.

## Learn 
### Event-Driven Architecture
- [Shopify Next Generation Events: Devs react to the biggest webhook overhaul in years](https://hookdeck.com/blog/shopify-next-generation-events-community-take.md): Community livestream recap of Shopify's Next Generation Events developer preview, which replaces topic-based webhooks with filterable, GraphQL-defined event subscriptions. Covers webhook volume and cost (AWS bills dominated by ingest), the kitchen-sink rollout, where complexity relocates under the new model, open reliability questions around delivery guarantees and reconciliation, migration strategies, GraphQL-based subscription management, and how the shift from 'webhooks' to 'events' echoes patterns seen at Stripe and beyond.
- [How Knock uses Orb webhooks for usage-based upgrade nudges](https://hookdeck.com/blog/knock-orb-usage-based-upgrade-nudges.md): Webhooks by Example episode one case study on using Orb subscription usage webhooks with enrichment, refetch-before-process, branching workflows, and idempotency for usage-based customer messaging.
- [Building Reliable MCP Servers: Handling Async Events and Webhooks](https://hookdeck.com/blog/mcp-event-gateway.md): Analysis of the async event handling gap in MCP server architecture. Covers MCP Tasks, Streamable HTTP transport limitations, MCP Gateway blind spots for inbound events, and how webhook infrastructure (Event Gateway) provides reliable ingestion, deduplication, retry, and observability for production MCP servers.
- [Webhooks at Scale: Best Practices and Lessons Learned](https://hookdeck.com/blog/webhooks-at-scale.md): Strategies and considerations for scaling webhook infrastructure to handle high-volume webhook traffic and complex routing requirements
- [Why Reliable Webhook Infrastructure Matters](https://hookdeck.com/blog/reliable-webhook-infrastructure.md): Comprehensive guide to building reliable webhook infrastructure covering architecture, error handling, monitoring, and best practices
- [Introducing The Event Destinations Initiative](https://hookdeck.com/blog/event-destinations-initiative.md): Details about Hookdeck's initiative to improve event destination handling and management capabilities
- [What are Event Destinations?](https://hookdeck.com/blog/event-destinations.md): Overview of event destination management and routing strategies for effective event-driven architecture implementations
- [Navigating Event-Driven Architecture: A Guide to Choosing the Right Infrastructure](https://hookdeck.com/blog/choosing-eda-infrastructure.md): Guide to selecting the right event-driven architecture infrastructure, covering message brokers, streaming platforms, event gateways, and storage options with recommendations based on solution needs
- [Aug 28-29th incident: Reaffirming our commitment to reliable async messaging infrastructure](https://hookdeck.com/blog/reliable-asynchronous-messaging-infrastructure.md): Guide to building robust asynchronous messaging systems with reliability, error handling, and scalability considerations
- [Detecting and Handling Delivery Errors in your Event-Driven Architecture](https://hookdeck.com/blog/detecting-error-handling-event-driven-architecture.md): Examines different types of message delivery errors in EDA, their mitigation strategies, and how to build robust error handling throughout the message lifecycle
- [Event-Driven Architecture Fundamentals and Common Pitfalls (and How to Avoid Them)](https://hookdeck.com/blog/event-driven-architecture-fundamentals-pitfalls.md): Comprehensive guide covering EDA fundamentals, message patterns, event design principles, and common pitfalls with solutions
- [Message Queues: Deep Dive](https://hookdeck.com/blog/message-queues-deep-dive.md): Advanced exploration of message queue architectures, patterns, and implementation considerations for production systems
- [Introduction to Messages Queues](https://hookdeck.com/blog/introduction-message-queue.md): Beginner-friendly introduction to message queues, covering what they are, how they work, and their role in distributed systems
- [Web Scalability for Beginners](https://hookdeck.com/blog/web-scalability-beginners.md): A comprehensive guide covering web scalability fundamentals, from handling growing user bases to implementing strategies like vertical/horizontal scaling, CDNs, and asynchronous processing with message queues
- [Introduction to Asynchronous Processing](https://hookdeck.com/blog/introduction-asynchronous-processing.md): Fundamental guide to asynchronous processing concepts, benefits, and implementation strategies for scalable applications

### Platform Guides
- [AWS SQS Alternatives for Webhooks: Hookdeck Event Gateway, Convoy, and Cloud Queues Compared](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/aws-sqs-alternatives-for-webhooks.md): In-depth comparison of AWS SQS alternatives for webhook ingestion and retries, analyzing Hookdeck Event Gateway, Convoy, Google Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ, and Postgres-backed queues across signature verification, per-source retry policies, dead-letter handling, replay, observability, and operational cost.
- [BullMQ Alternatives for Webhook Retries: Hookdeck Event Gateway, pg-boss, Cloud Queues, and Convoy Compared](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/bullmq-alternatives-for-webhook-retries.md): In-depth comparison of BullMQ alternatives for webhook retries in Node.js applications, analyzing Hookdeck Event Gateway, pg-boss, Bee-Queue, AWS SQS, Google Cloud Tasks, and Convoy across signature verification, per-source retry policies, failed-payload visibility, serverless fit, replay, and operational cost.
- [Inngest Alternatives: Hookdeck Event Gateway, Trigger.dev, Temporal, and Restate Compared](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/inngest-alternatives.md): In-depth comparison of Inngest alternatives across two layers — webhook ingestion and durable execution, analyzing Hookdeck Event Gateway, Trigger.dev, Temporal, and Restate on signature verification, durable step execution, language and SDK fit, self-hostability, pricing, and observability.
- [RequestBin Alternatives for Testing Webhooks: Hookdeck Console, webhook.site, Beeceptor, and Pipedream Compared](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/requestbin-alternatives.md): In-depth comparison of RequestBin alternatives for testing and inspecting webhooks, analyzing Hookdeck Console, webhook.site, Beeceptor, Pipedream, and ngrok's request inspector across inspection depth, persistence, replay-to-localhost, provider sample libraries, team workflows, and the path to production.
- [Sidekiq Alternatives for Webhook Retries: Hookdeck Event Gateway, Solid Queue, GoodJob, and Cloud Queues Compared](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/sidekiq-alternatives-for-webhook-retries.md): In-depth comparison of Sidekiq alternatives for webhook retries in Rails applications, analyzing Hookdeck Event Gateway, Solid Queue, GoodJob, AWS SQS, and Convoy across signature verification, per-source retry policies, failed-payload visibility, replay, and operational footprint.
- [Shopify Next Generation Events: What's Changing and How to Migrate](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/shopify-next-generation-events-migration-guide.md): Migration guide for Shopify Next Generation Events (Developer Preview, unstable API, Product and Customer topics only): TOML event subscriptions with field-level triggers, custom Admin GraphQL query payloads, query filters, and a fields_changed array; side-by-side comparison with classic Admin API webhook subscriptions; a six-step migration playbook (audit, rank by noise, translate, dual-run, update idempotency/HMAC, handle the download-envelope shape); plus receiving events with Hookdeck for observability, filtering, routing, local development, and replay.
- [Migrating from a RabbitMQ-backed webhook pipeline to Hookdeck](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/rabbitmq-to-hookdeck-migration.md): Five-step phased migration plan from a RabbitMQ-backed webhook pipeline to Hookdeck Event Gateway: shadow ingest, mirror to production, flip the source, repeat per source in increasing order of stakes, and decommission. Covers what to keep versus replace, per-step rollback paths, and the common mistakes teams make.
- [What RabbitMQ doesn't give you for webhooks (and what you'll end up building)](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/rabbitmq-webhook-shortcomings.md): Walkthrough of the webhook-specific work RabbitMQ does not cover: the HTTP ingestion tier, per-source signature verification, source-aware retries, idempotency, lifecycle observability, replay and backfill, and transformation. Explains why the queue is roughly 20% of a webhook system and what a managed webhook gateway bundles around it.
- [Migrating Redis-backed webhook handling to Hookdeck Event Gateway](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/redis-to-hookdeck-migration.md): Phased migration plan from Redis-backed webhook handling (BullMQ, Sidekiq, RQ, Celery, Redis Streams, or hand-rolled LPUSH/BRPOP) to Hookdeck Event Gateway. Covers the three starting shapes, what to keep versus replace, a five-phase rollout with per-phase rollback, and the mistakes teams make.
- [Why Redis is a great cache, but a bad webhook queue](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/redis-webhook-queue-teardown.md): Technical teardown of Redis-backed webhook ingestion. Examines the LPUSH/BRPOP job-queue pattern, Redis Streams, and Pub/Sub against the realities of webhook traffic (durability modes, memory eviction, asynchronous replication loss) and argues that the webhook edge needs a layer Redis was never built to be.
- [Building AI code review with GitHub and Claude](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/building-ai-code-review-with-github-and-claude.md): Tutorial: GitHub pull_request webhooks via Hookdeck to a Claude code review handler with filters (skip drafts, bots, oversized PRs), rate limiting, retries, and replay; reviews fan back to GitHub as inline comments via a second Hookdeck connection.

- [Why most webhook-triggered agents don't need a workflow engine](https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/most-webhook-agents-dont-need-a-workflow-engine.md): Argues that most webhook-triggered agents are LLM-in-a-handler patterns (model call + DB write + notification), not real workflows. Durable runtimes like Inngest, Trigger.dev, Hatchet, and Temporal earn their keep for multi-step workflows with waitpoints, compensations, long-running state, or scheduled follow-ups — not for three-function handlers. Covers the real failure modes (HTTP timeouts, crashes, transient downstream errors), what a queue plus handler gets you, the costs of runtime adoption (per-execution pricing, SDK lock-in, language lock-in), a checklist for when a runtime is warranted, and a YAGNI blueprint: Hookdeck gateway + idempotent handler + meaningful status codes.

Gateways solve ingress: signature verification, dedup, durable queuing, retries, replay. Runtimes solve execution: checkpointed steps, per-step retries, long-running tasks, waitpoints, scheduling. Covers failure modes, when to use one vs both, common misconceptions, and how the two layers compose.
